Neha / team,

Quick initial findings from a rapid check of serving logs and policy propagation:
- Around 08:45 PDT an updated quota/burst policy for the BrightLine tenant propagated from control-plane. The policy lowered the burst window from 300s to 60s and tightened the per-second steady-state QPS (policy id: bp-6442).
- Runtime started enforcing safety-valve logic that disables prefix-KV caching for high QPS prefixes when X-Burst-Window < 120s; that interaction was unintended for this tenant because their traffic pattern is high short-burst (campaign ramp). The result is many requests now miss the cache path and get routed through a stricter quota check, causing immediate 429s when bursts exceed the shortened window.
- I see a sequence where X-Quota-Remaining goes to 0 after a few high-concurrency requests and then rapid successive requests are dropped.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Roll back the policy to the previous bp-6339 (burst window 300s) — fastest, low risk.
2) Temporarily raise the per-tenant emergency headroom (bump soft quota by +40%) and relax the cache disable rule for 2 hours.
3) Route BrightLine traffic to dedicated slower-path nodes that have more permissive burst handling (requires infra change, ~30-45m).

I'll start a rollback if we have verbal approval. Also collecting detailed traces to quantify customer impact. Recommend we offer a partial credit for the incident if rollback doesn't fully mitigate user errors.

Karthik
Senior SRE — Inference Runtime
